summary: Pass 51 promotes native.save-coordination from UNKNOWN to STRONG by separating proven Classic/Worldgroup persistence ownership from Reforged's generic prepare/commit/rollback coordinator. Native WCC configuration retains 60-second Player data and 300-second Buffer data save clocks. MajorMUD uses retained Worldgroup DFA contexts and explicit insert/update/delete calls; WGSERVER exposes begin/end/abort/unlock transaction operations, stages variable-length mutations in shared buffer 0x00467CA4, records synchronous BTRCALL status, and delegates physical durability to WBTRV32/W32MKDE. W32MKDE proves write-back dirty state, pending-write counters, synchronous FlushFileBuffers barriers, and startup recovery artifact ownership. Exact MajorMUD player/world participant order, exact Buffer data record-family mapping, transaction grouping selected by the module, ordinary-save flush durability, and shutdown-save ordering remain unresolved and fail closed.
classificationPolicy: Native timing/storage/transaction ownership receives parity credit only at the layer actually proven. RuntimeSaveCoordinationService ordering, prepare/commit phases, reverse rollback, generation snapshots, and JSON atomic replacement are Reforged policy and receive zero Classic parity credit.

nativeSaveClocks.nonClaim: The 300-second Buffer data prompt does not identify the exact MajorMUD record families or prove ordering relative to Player data.

majorMudDfaBoundary.finding: MajorMUD imports distinct mutation calls and explicit reset/release operations, but does not directly import the host transaction exports in the recovered family.

worldgroupPhysicalBoundary.finding: Insert/update wrappers stage caller data in the shared host buffer before synchronous BTRCALL; nonzero statuses enter Worldgroup error paths.
worldgroupPhysicalBoundary.nonClaim: The existence of host transaction exports does not prove which MajorMUD save operations are grouped into one transaction.

mkdeDurabilityBoundary.writeBehavior: successful ordinary writes can remain pending behind MKDE dirty state; proven explicit/conditional flush wrappers synchronously flush at selected boundaries
mkdeDurabilityBoundary.nonClaim: Exact transaction-log bytes, replay semantics, and whether every ordinary MajorMUD save reaches an immediate flush are not proven.
